Cayuga

Cayuga is one of the Haudenosaunee peoples. This starting path brings together a dated Cayuga council publication from New York and language work at Six Nations of the Grand River; those contexts should not be collapsed into a single present government.

Read the sources [3] Cayuga Nation Council / Unity Council; hosted by the Haudenosaunee Confederacy [4] Six Nations Polytechnic

01

Identity and context

Cayuga is one of the Haudenosaunee nations. Different Cayuga communities and governing institutions require distinct treatment.

Read the sources [1] Cayuga Nation

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Gayogo̱hó꞉nǫʼ identity, language, homelands and Haudenosaunee relationships. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] Cayuga Nation [2] cayuganation-nsn.gov [3] Cayuga Nation Council / Unity Council; hosted by the Haudenosaunee Confederacy

03

A schoolhouse account from 2014

A December 2014 council newsletter describes a schoolhouse intended for all-age language and cultural learning. A quoted speaker connects this work with Cayuga Lake and people returning home. The article records the project’s intentions at that time; it does not establish present operation or resolve competing council claims.

Read the sources [3] Cayuga Nation Council / Unity Council; hosted by the Haudenosaunee Confederacy

04

Community-based language research

Six Nations Polytechnic’s 2016–2017 study investigated adult language learning through community participation, focus groups and questionnaires. Its recommendations connect classroom instruction with speaking in everyday community settings. These selected methods and goals provide a research entry point, rather than a guarantee about how quickly any learner becomes fluent.

Read the sources [4] Six Nations Polytechnic

05

A higher-education route

Six Nations Polytechnic’s published programme describes separate Cayuga and Mohawk language streams, alongside community, practice and research-methods study. This is one educational institution’s public route into language work, not a description of every Cayuga community or a substitute for community-specific history.

Read the sources [5] Six Nations Polytechnic

Gayogoho:nǫ’ News, December 31, 2014 — cultural schoolhouse article, p5 ↗

The dated community newsletter describes a schoolhouse intended for intergenerational language and cultural learning. Its quoted speakers connect the project with Cayuga Lake and returning home. Read it as this council’s 2014 perspective.

Pathways to Creating Onkwehonwehnéha Speakers at Six Nations of The Grand River Territory — selected study sections ↗

A community-based 2016–2017 study examines adult language learning, programme coordination and opportunities to use language beyond classes. Its Six Nations focus is a specific community context, not a universal account of every Cayuga or Mohawk community.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual 96-page PDF: title/acknowledgments and abstract, PDF pp1–2 and7; selected background, project goals and study conduct pp8–11; selected focus-group/questionnaire methodology pp28–31.
